solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Living standard

definitions.meaning: a living is a livelihood, the job that keeps food on the table
standard here means basic, ordinary, everyday

explanation.walkthrough: 'Living standard' reads as one economic phrase, but it splits into two separate definitions of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both one's basic livelihood and anything routine or fundamental, so it covers a living and a standard.

clue.text: Mix up compound and isomer

indicators.note: compound as a verb means to combine and mix, so the letters are blended

explanation.surface: A chemistry instruction: mix the compound with an isomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' and 'isomer' make a chemistry scene, but 'compound' is the verb signalling the anagram of AND ISOMER.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in a random order is to shuffle or mix them up.

clue.text: Hand out bags to the audience?

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners, so take the sound of the phrase

parts.note: bags means lots, plenty, as in 'bags of time'

explanation.surface: Giving out bags to theatregoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' is informal for 'a lot'; 'to the audience' makes A LOT sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute shares or portions is to apportion or give them out.

clue.text: Something of Chelsea observed during a trip — wealth!

indicators.note: observed during means seen in the middle of the other part

parts.note: to trip, as in trip the light fantastic, is to dance
a Chelsea bun is a sweet currant roll

explanation.surface: A Chelsea fan spots something on a jaunt and cries out about riches.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea bun is a spiral currant pastry, named after the London district; 'trip' is a dance, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth and plenty both mean having a great quantity of something.

clue.text: Going uphill, lawn proves alluring

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sward is an expanse of grass or turf

explanation.surface: Walking up a sloping lawn is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going uphill' reverses SWARD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pulls in crowds or attention attracts them, which is what being alluring does.

clue.text: Badly ruined, men weaken

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are damaged and put back in disorder

explanation.surface: Men who have been ruined are left feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' signals the anagram of RUINED MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To subvert or erode something gradually from beneath is to weaken it.

clue.text: Fish in bottom of net, thrashing

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a thrashing is a heavy defeat, a rout

explanation.surface: A fish thrashing about at the bottom of a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashing' pictures the fish flapping, but it is the noun meaning a crushing defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater game fish of the salmon family is a common catch.

clue.text: US farmer made swift progress, he being in credit

parts.note: to run is to make swift progress, past tense ran

indicators.note: being in says the word he sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: An American farmer did well, finding himself in the black.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American West, a cattle or livestock farmer works a ranch.

clue.text: Server keeping time precisely

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: a spoon is used for serving food

explanation.surface: A waiter who is exactly punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' suggests a waiter or a tennis player; it is a serving spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly right or accurate is the informal sense of the phrase, a synonym of precisely.

clue.text: Board bound to flip about pension, ultimately

indicators.note: about means around, so the flipped word goes round the other letter
flipping turns the word for bound back to front

parts.note: to bound is to leap

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of pension

explanation.surface: A pensions board is obliged to reverse course on its pension policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to flip' turns LEAP into PAEL; 'about' puts it round N, the last letter of 'pension'.
explanation.definitionFit: A board and a panel are both groups of people appointed to judge, advise or decide.

clue.text: Changeable — switch positions?

definitions.meaning: changeable means fluctuating, going through good and bad spells
a light switch has two settings, on with one flick and off with the other

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as playful: a switch's two settings are literally the two directions named.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluctuating mood or fortune rises and falls, and a toggle switch flicks one way or the other.

clue.text: Cart finally went off, and moved at a fair pace

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word cart

parts.note: food that went off has rotted

explanation.surface: A horse and cart: something in the cart spoiled, but the horse kept up a decent speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Trotting is a horse's gait faster than walking but slower than cantering, a moderate brisk speed.

clue.text: Cancel score

definitions.meaning: to cancel, as when a runner is withdrawn from a race
to score is to mark a surface with a line or groove

explanation.definitionFit: A horse withdrawn from a race is struck off the list, and scoring a surface means marking it with a sharp point.

clue.text: Beastly sound actually audible

indicators.note: audible says the word is to be heard rather than spelt, so we write what it sounds like

parts.note: nay can mean 'indeed, or rather', strengthening what came before, as in 'many, nay most'

explanation.surface: A noise made by some animal can truly be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audible' turns NAY into its sound-alike; 'Beastly' means 'of a beast', not 'nasty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's whinny is the call a beast makes, so it is literally a beastly sound.

clue.text: When heard, secrete diamonds observed in compound

indicators.note: when heard says these words are to be listened to, not spelt

parts.note: secrete is hide, diamonds are rocks in slang, and observed is eyed, giving hide rocks eyed

explanation.surface: Something hides gems that someone spotted inside a chemical substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When heard' makes HIDE ROCKS EYED (secrete, diamonds, observed) sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydroxides, such as caustic soda, are chemical compounds containing the OH group.

clue.text: One selecting an idiot, perhaps, in critic

parts.note: a nit is a fool or idiot in British slang
someone who picks or chooses is a picker

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a fool, maybe, shows up among the reviewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that choosing a fool is only one reading of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant who finds fault with trivial details is a petty critic.

clue.text: Child is real tricky, you can bet on it!

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are twisted into a difficult arrangement

explanation.surface: A child is genuinely difficult, and that is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you can bet on it!' sounds like 'certainly', but it defines a betting machine; 'tricky' signals the anagram of IS REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tote machine pools bets at a racecourse and calculates the odds, so punters wager through it.

clue.text: Criminal joke, one having a lie down?

parts.note: to kid is to joke or tease
someone taking a nap is a napper

explanation.surface: A criminal joke about someone taking a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abducts a person for ransom is a type of criminal.

clue.text: Most secure, building stateside

indicators.note: building suggests putting the letters together in a new construction

explanation.surface: The safest construction work is going on in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' signals the anagram of STATESIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmest and least wobbly, the superlative of an adjective for stable, matches 'most secure'.

clue.text: Down — that's feathered

definitions.meaning: to down a drink is to gulp it
something with feathers is a bird, here a fork-tailed one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like soft feathers, matching 'feathered', but it is the verb meaning to gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulping a drink down the throat is one sense, and a fork-tailed migratory bird is the other.

clue.text: Wood cut, knock over cherry tree

indicators.note: cut means its last letter is chopped off

parts.note: elm is a kind of wood

indicators.note: knocking something over upends it, so in a down-the-page reading the word runs backwards

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A woodcutter knocks down a cherry tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks ELM to EL; 'knock over' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries used for cordial and wine.

clue.text: Secured by band, papers being carried

indicators.note: secured by means held inside the band

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: Documents held in a rubber band are carried along.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger in a car or on a horse is borne along, which is being carried.

clue.text: Sanction range alongside software tool

indicators.note: alongside places the two parts next to each other

parts.note: an app is a piece of software
to range is to roam or rove

explanation.surface: Authorise a cooker range along with some software utility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' wants to be a noun (a cooker or set of options); here it is the verb 'wander'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise or endorse it officially.

clue.text: Authority in parliament often weak, evidently rubbish leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters, heading each of the following words

explanation.surface: A grumble that parliament is weak and its leaders plainly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like party leaders but picks the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and authority both mean the right or ability to control others.

clue.text: Something going on still, heading for trouble

parts.note: still and even are both intensifiers, as in 'still better' and 'even better'

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: Something is still happening and it is headed for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion or happening is something that takes place.

clue.text: Haul girl back, one going slowly

indicators.note: back says the combined words are written backwards

parts.note: to haul is to drag
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone drags a girl back because she is dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses DRAGGAL as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler who falls behind others is one who moves slowly.

clue.text: Measure right round

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to measure the right way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right round' looks like it describes measuring; 'round' signals an anagram of RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The measurement around the middle of a body or tree trunk is its circumference.

clue.text: Poor quality rum wino sells

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters come out oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A drunk sells rum of poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink a wino might sell, but here it is the adjective 'odd', the anagram signal for WINO SELLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being humble or low in rank is the condition of having poor status, a poor quality in the sense of trait.

clue.text: Wiser in the end, I turn out mature

indicators.note: in the end selects the closing letter of wiser

parts.note: to turn out a book or article is to write it, to pen it

explanation.surface: Older and wiser, I end up grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' is the verb 'produce', as a writer turns out a novel, so it gives PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or cheese that matures develops fully, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Choristers were assembled where triennial choir festival staged?

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters are reassembled into a new order

explanation.surface: Singers gathered at the venue of a choir festival held every three years.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Choirs Festival rotates among Worcester, Hereford and Gloucester cathedrals, so Worcester hosts it every third year; strictly the county is a loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county containing Worcester hosts the Three Choirs Festival once in each three-year cycle.
